name: Grip Strip from Buggy Choke
summary: Moving to Side Control after a Buggy Choke requires the top player to clear the bottom player's head-and-arm loop before establishing the next control.
description: Grip Strip from Buggy Choke opens the bottom player's arm-and-leg loop. Recover neck space and stable top frames before settling into side control again.
overview:
The top player is the choke defender even though this transition calls the moving player its attacker. Changing pins does not itself prove that the choke is gone. Clear the arm-and-leg loop first, and do not lift or slam the partner to escape.

Watch for an arm reaching past your head and connecting to the same-side leg. Avoid lifting, dropping, or twisting the partner's trapped leg to force an escape. Use safe inside frames before the arm-to-leg loop fully closes; do not pull or twist the partner's knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Kade and Tye Ruotolo — OG Buggy Choke](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zixbOyLpoOc); [Jay Rodriguez — three Buggy Choke mistakes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MjKERx4N4mY).

flashcards.answer: Watch for an arm reaching past your head and connecting to the same-side leg.

Their hip frame below your ribs

flashcards.question: Grip Strip from Buggy Choke (top): Why keep your base on the mat during the strip?
flashcards.answer: Maintain grounded support and address the early connection without lifting or using the linked knee as leverage.
flashcards.answer_line: Lifting them risks an attached fall

Standing proves elbow-knee release

flashcards.question: Grip Strip from Buggy Choke (top): What is the useful timing for an inside frame?
flashcards.answer: Use safe inside frames before the arm-to-leg loop fully closes; do not pull or twist the partner's knee.

plausible: After neck is tight under pressure
After turning head in the shut loop
trap: Once elbow presses into raised knee

flashcards.question: Grip Strip from Buggy Choke (top): The grip opens but the loop stays snug. What must you verify?
flashcards.answer: A change in hand grip does not itself establish escape; verify release of the head-and-arm enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: Head and arm are free to withdraw

plausible: Their hips remain pinned to the mat
Far knee can step around their head
trap: Clasp open, elbow still hooks knee

flashcards.question: Grip Strip from Buggy Choke (top): After clearance, where should side-control attachment act?
flashcards.answer: Establish Side Control only after the head is free. Keep the shoulders and hips controlled while moving outside the legs.
flashcards.answer_line: Upper body and hips, outside legs

plausible: Shoulders, inside knee still between
Hip line, chest off their shoulders
trap: Near wrist, hip line turns freely

flashcards.question: Grip Strip from Buggy Choke (top): What should precede settling a crossface?
flashcards.answer: Chest and shoulder pressure belong to the new side pin after loop release, not to forcing the old choke apart.

plausible: Drive pressure through trapped neck
Drop chest with their knee inside
trap: Hand open, elbow linked to knee

flashcards.question: Buggy grip strip (top): Why does an opened hand grip still require a head-and-arm clearance check?
flashcards.answer: A changed hand grip can leave the head-and-arm loop close around the neck. Verify that the whole enclosure is open before extracting the head or changing pins.
flashcards.answer_line: Leg and upper arm may trap the neck

plausible: Hand release proves elbow-knee gap
Chest pin pulls neck out of the loop
trap: Hip turn frees neck before arm moves

defender.name: Grip Strip from Buggy Choke Defender
defender.description: Grip Strip from Buggy Choke (defender): Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg. Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg.
defender.overview:
The top player is the choke defender even though this transition calls the moving player its attacker. Changing pins does not itself prove that the choke is gone. Clear the arm-and-leg loop first, and do not lift or slam the partner to escape.

Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg. Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg. Shorten the connection through body position, not by pulling the foot hard toward the face.

Close space with the arm, leg, and torso while avoiding twisting force on your own knee. Use a disengaging opponent's movement to insert frames and knees if the choke is lost. Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

When the grip is stripped, keep an inside shoulder frame and use a short hip escape to recover a knee. Abandoning the old loop early preserves guard-recovery space that disappears once the top player settles the pin.
key_principles: Build the angle: Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg.
Enclose head and arm: Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg.
Keep elbow near knee: Shorten the connection through body position, not by pulling the foot hard toward the face.
Use the torso connection: Close space with the arm, leg, and torso while avoiding twisting force on your own knee.
Recover guard when space opens: Use a disengaging opponent's movement to insert frames and knees if the choke is lost.
Release if lifted: Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam.

flashcards.question: Grip Strip from Buggy Choke (bottom): What body angle makes your hand-leg connection easier?
flashcards.answer: Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Partly on ribs, hips shifted out

plausible: Flat, reaching elbow far from knee
On ribs, hip extends away from knee
trap: Flat, shoulder away from raised knee

flashcards.question: Grip Strip from Buggy Choke (bottom): What must remain enclosed for the Buggy threat to exist?
flashcards.answer: The loop must contain the top player's head and one arm, not merely connect your hand to your leg.
flashcards.answer_line: The opponent's head and one arm

plausible: Only their elbow, head outside
Head only, both arms left outside
trap: Your thigh, wherever their head is

flashcards.question: Grip Strip from Buggy Choke (bottom): How should you preserve a compact elbow-knee connection?
flashcards.answer: Shorten the connection through body position, not by pulling the foot hard toward the face.
flashcards.answer_line: Use side angle, not foot pulling

plausible: Pull foot across a stationary knee
Straighten linking arm against strip
trap: Extend ribs away to tighten loop

flashcards.question: Grip Strip from Buggy Choke (bottom): What action closes space as you hold the loop?
flashcards.answer: Shoulder-to-hip shortening supplies closure while the arm and leg enclose the opponent.

plausible: Lift the shoulder away from the hip
Move hips away, keep shoulder high

flashcards.question: Grip Strip from Buggy Choke (bottom): Your grip is stripped. What should replace the lost loop?
flashcards.answer: Use a disengaging opponent's movement to insert frames and knees if the choke is lost.

plausible: Both hands reach for the same foot
Turn away with near elbow flared
trap: Shift hips, leave near knee outside
